subject: Re: HeliosCare model-eval onramp — data format & scorer criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@helioscare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (HeliosCare eval on Redwood)

Thanks for the call earlier, Sam — good session. Recap + proposed next steps below so we keep momentum and scope the pilot clearly.

Quick recap:
- Goal: run customer-specific quality evals on Redwood to validate model fit for triage/enrichment workflows (clinical note summarization + structured extraction).
- Primary success metrics: extraction F1 (per-field), summarization ROUGE-L, hallucination rate < 3% for high-risk fields.

Proposed onramp items (actionable):
1) Data & access from your side — sample dataset in JSONL (one record per prompt) with fields: id, input_text, expected_output, labels (per-field), and sensitivity tags. Prefer S3 link, gzipped.
2) Prompt bank — we’ll run a representative prompt set (attached prompt_bank_v1.jsonl).
3) Baseline model shortlist — we recommend running the following during the first sweep: Redwood-turbo-3.1 (hosted), Llama-2-70B-chat (8-bit quant), and a smaller 7B variant for latency comparisons. We'll surface token cost and latency per model.
4) Scoring & guardrails — initial rubric attached; roughly: exact-match & F1 for structured fields, ROUGE-L + BERTScore for summaries, and a binary hallucination check for PHI fields. We flag any model with >5% regression vs baseline on critical fields.
5) Timeline — baseline pass (one-shot scoring) in 10 business days after we get S3 access + sample 500 records. Full eval (5k records, stratified) within 4 weeks.
6) Privacy & compliance — confirm whether data needs additional PII redaction on our side, and whether routing must stay in us-west-2.

Next steps (owners):
- Sam (HeliosCare): share S3 path + any access IAM role, or upload the 500-sample tarball to the link above. (ASAP, prefer by Fri 2/20)
- Ben: prepare pilot commercial note (pilot pricing & term sheet).
- Monica: review scoring rubric and confirm any extra label fields you want included (e.g., patient_consent flag).

Attachments: dataset_sample.jsonl (schema), prompt_bank_v1.jsonl, eval_runbook_v0.2.pdf (scoring thresholds & regression policy).

If that all looks good, we’ll queue the baseline run and share the initial benchmark dashboard (latency/cost/quality) within 48 hours of ingest.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sam Green <sam.green@helioscare.com>

Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@helioscare.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (HeliosCare eval on Redwood)

Thanks, Rishi — that captures the call. Two quick clarifications:

1) We have uploaded a 500-record sample to s3://helioscare-eval/samples/500_sample_v1.jsonl.gz — I’ll grant an IAM role to redwood-eval@helioscare with GetObject/ListObject by end of day.
2) For PHI, we prefer Redwood to perform evaluation in-region (us-west-2) with our KMS keys. We will mark any field with PHI in the labels.

Also — for safety scoring, can you include a check that flags PHI leakage (model outputs containing patient identifiers) separately from content-quality metrics? That’s a must for our security team.

One more ask: are you able to run the initial sweep on Dedicated (we have strict SLAs and would like to compare hosted vs dedicated latency/cost)? If not immediately, run on hosted and we can plan a Dedicated run after baseline.

Regards,
Sam
Director of ML Ops, HeliosCare
sam.green@helioscare.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@helioscare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Eval runbook & scorer thresholds (update)

Sam — added a couple of concrete thresholds and the regression alert policy inline so your security and compliance teams can review quickly. See the attached eval_runbook_v0.2.pdf for full detail; summary below.

Scoring summary (baseline pass):
- Structured extraction: per-field F1. Acceptance threshold = 0.78 average across critical fields (diagnosis_code, medication, dosage).
- Summarization: ROUGE-L F1 >= 0.62 measured on 3-reference subset.
- Hallucination/PHI leakage: binary check on patient identifiers; any instance triggers a manual review. Target <= 0.03 (3%) for high-risk fields.
- Latency & cost: median tail latency (p95) under 450ms for the smaller 7B; provide p50/p95/99 and cost-per-1k tokens for each model.

Regression policy:
- If any model shows >5 percentage point drop on a critical field vs the first baseline, we auto-create a regression ticket and notify the HeliosCare contact list. We keep a rolling 30-day eval window for trend analysis.

Data format & sample (attached dataset_sample.jsonl):
- One JSON object per line with fields: id, input_text, expected_output, labels (json array), sensitivity_tags (json array), source_id.
- Please include a small mapping file if your labels use internal codes.

Operational notes:
- KMS/in-region: we’ll run the job in us-west-2 and accept your role-based S3 access; please add redwood-eval@helioscare (specified IAM) to the bucket policy.
- Dedicated run: we can schedule a Dedicated comparison in week 3 of the pilot; Monica and Ben, please start sizing with expected concurrency.

Next check-in: I’ll kick the baseline job once I have S3 access and confirm the IAM role. We’ll share an initial dashboard (read-only) and a short findings memo after the first 500-record pass.

—
Rishi
From: Sam Green <sam.green@helioscare.com>

Sam
